processing: Large-leaf tea given a comparatively light wet-pile fermentation, enough to remove raw pu-erh's bitterness while keeping some of its liveliness, then tightly pressed into a tuo.
harvest_season: Not sold by picking: it is a factory blend, and the year on the wrapper marks production.
appearance_dry: A firm, tightly pressed 100 g dark-brown bowl-shaped tuo.
appearance_wet: Soft, chestnut-brown large-leaf pieces, some broken from the tight pressing.
taste_profile: Smooth and full with caramel, malt-syrup and woody notes, and a thick, sweet aftertaste; some batches carry noticeable smoke.

brewing.notes: Break the tuo carefully with a pick, since it is pressed tight, and rinse once. If a young batch tastes smoky, air it for a while before judging it.

vintage_note: Sold by production year, usually as 100 g tuos, often in five-tuo bags of 500 g. The 2005 and 2006 productions are the famous ones and still command high prices; later years such as 2017, 2019 and 2022 are made to the same named recipe. Smoke varies between years, and some drinkers find it fades after a few years.
description:
V93 is Dayi's premium ripe tuo, a 100 g bowl that became one of the most expensive ripe teas on the market soon after it arrived. Its appeal is simple: it drinks well every day, yet keeps more life in it than many ripe teas.

The fermentation is deliberately on the lighter side, breaking down raw pu-erh's bitterness while leaving some of its stimulation and returning sweetness. The tuo itself is pressed hard, so it opens slowly in the pot and may need several steeps to get going.

The cup is smooth and full, with caramel, malt syrup and wood, and a thick, sweet finish. Drinkers disagree about smoke: it stands out in some years and is hardly there in others. A good starting point is about 8 g in 120 ml of water just off the boil, with short steeps.

Buy with the year in mind, because the early productions and the recent ones are priced very differently. If smoke bothers you, taste a sample of the year before buying a bag.
history:
V93 was first released in 2005 by Menghai Tea Factory, and quickly gained a following as a premium everyday ripe tea. The 2005 and 2006 productions remain the ones collectors chase.

The tea has continued in later years; recent productions are described as following the 2005 recipe, in the same 100 g tuo format.
